sourceDifferences.finding: Cut drawer passes Z-z+1 (never zero); BridgePierVoxel alpha-at-zero branch is not reached by this caller.
Clock invokes the queued callback before removeMin. Self/other cancellation can remove the current entry and cause the following entry to be removed instead.
SingleRailRoad.build(equal endpoints) proceeds to invalid Direction; UI excludes it. Route preview returns empty while remove quote returns zero.
Bridge support teardown ignores its owner argument; slope entity removal excludes BridgePierVoxel and leaves elected piers.
StoppingAtSignal is not assigned by Train.clockHandler; all positive waits set StoppingAtStation. Default dwell is 30 minutes despite the one-hour comment.
Bridge predicate does not require water despite its comment; tunnel removal excludes its final endpoint. UI reachability/geometry guards must accompany direct domain calls.
Signal needsToDrawAfter predicate is used for drawBefore; its negation is used for drawAfter. Preserve actual calls in source expectations.
Train.place follows loc += direction without slope z transitions; traversal across a ramp is not equivalent to movement and can fail placement.

exavDifferences.finding: Direction indices/vectors, integer projection/picking and all 60 pattern/16 support definitions retained. Direction display names are Japanese; host drawing namespaces changed.
Construction 6000000 * (height<0 ? -2*height : height+1), height=z-ground. Removal 2000000 * count * (abs(endZ-water)+1). Long quote/aggregate; individual int products still need overflow decisions.
Construction 40000000 * (height<0 ? -2*height : height+1), height=baseZ-water; removal 8000000*(abs(baseZ+1-water)+1). Eight-cell legality and slope frame/z-transition geometry retained.

New build/removal accounting and occupied TrainCar removal guards. Bridge/girder precharge entire inclusive route even when occupied cells are skipped; tunnel charges only created/removed cells and still excludes final removal endpoint. Preserve as source differences pending portable transaction decisions.

-999 forwards without reversal, -1000 reverses and forwards; other negative waits reverse. Yard departure rings bell but skips boarding for either sentinel. Outside counter 50 unloads but skips reload while forwarding.

Movement charges on successful movements 1,5,9,...: (length*20+passenger/20)*2000. Fare r*fare*distance*2. Seated capacity falls back per car when invalid, packed capacity = seated+2*(capacity-seated). Reverse wrapper copies seated capacity. Sale returns price/(wholeYears+2) only with boughtTime.

First placement uses native interval. At callback completion Inside->Inside uses pre-move head location (also on blocked retry); exit and outside-return use native interval. Low always 4; medium native only if exactly 4 else 3; fast native only if exactly 3/4 else 2. This is not a generic max(native,limit). Priority low,medium,fast if malformed lists overlap.

Both host ranges now 8. Thin roof optional, middle indices length/4 <= i < length-length/4; fat constructor resets only its local withRoof argument, no new roof drawing. Concrete/brown/green passageway and stair arrays; changed drawAfter overload no longer overrides ordinary two-argument RailRoad.drawAfter.

Tick/queue order and minute/calendar constants retained. Clock adds shallow Clone, Time adds gameStartTime, fixed holiday/vacation predicates and Japanese weekday/display strings; TimeLength adds integer division. PriorityQueue.setValueComparer now assigns vc; callback cancellation issue remains.

Car pose/frame and six traffic passes retained. SimpleSprite blits _size. Station labels use configured fonts/colors; recursive train labels render afterwards only for Inside heads, offset Y=-8. Catalog preview searches 5,6..17,4..1; it is not a movement oracle. AbstractLineController cost display calls road helpers even for special rail; must not be used as authoritative rail quote.
Occupied signal removal rejects any car; source pass-predicate inversion retained.

openWork: Expand offline gallery to changed girder artwork and three platform/passageway styles, both roofs/widths/stairs and cuts. The regenerated 152 rail/car scenes do not cover these additions.

P0-06 must derive independent movement/boarding/calendar/cost cases; P1-P5 implement and verify runtime routes, timers, train state, picking and full-world rendering. Native/runtime captures and P10 save continuation remain unverified.

chains.title: Picture loading, sprite anchors, native blit and effects

steps.finding: Missing seasonal day uses spring day. Missing seasonal night uses that season's automatic night only when its day was explicitly supplied, otherwise spring night. getNightOverride inspects only the first nested override; authored night bypasses automatic darkening. Surface reload is lazy, and the loader returns the color key.
acceptanceCases: PIC-01: explicit summer day without summer night -> generated summer night; absent summer day/night -> spring pair.
PIC-02: first nested override is summer, later sibling is night -> base getNightOverride returns null; do not treat every later night as effective.
steps.disposition: Source expectation; implement and verify in the named slice. Defects require an explicit port decision, not implicit fidelity.

steps.finding: Automatic night is channel /4, with (8,0,0)->(255,8,8), (0,8,0)->(252,243,148), (0,0,8)->(255,227,99). Native 555/565 quantization differs from 24/32-bit; unknown 16-bit returns E_NOTIMPL. Managed loader ignores returned status. Raw night crops and day compositions do not verify this conversion.
acceptanceCases: PIC-03: compare ordinary colors, marker lights and transformed color key in a named pixel format.
PIC-04: verify clock 05:59->06:00,17:59->18:00, forced mode and surface-loss reload. A season boundary alone does not dirty pictures until another reset.
steps.disposition: Source expectation; implement and verify in the named slice. Defects require an explicit port decision, not implicit fidelity.

steps.finding: Crop and anchor survive wrapper migration: destination=point-offset, source=origin..origin+size, matching destination/source clipping. Shape uses keyed silhouette; alpha uses native keyed approximately-half blend, not bitmap alpha. 24/32-bit channels compute floor(dst/2)+floor(src/2). ColorMappedSprite/HueTransformSprite override draw only, so inherited shape/alpha bypass their color transforms.
acceptanceCases: BLIT-01: clipped 32x32 sprite with nonzero anchor must shift the source rectangle by the same clip amount.
BLIT-02: non-key source channel 3 over destination 5 -> 1+2=3 in 24/32-bit half blend; source key leaves destination unchanged.
BLIT-03: transformed normal draw versus inherited untransformed alpha/shape must have distinct expectations.
steps.disposition: Source expectation; implement and verify in the named slice. Defects require an explicit port decision, not implicit fidelity.

steps.finding: Alpha set masks portions occluded by cells xx<=x, yy>=y, zz>=z using projected offsets to avoid double blending. DirectSprite.offset recursively returns offset instead of _offset. Native Surface.HitTest returns equality with key, allows x==Width/y==Height, and SimpleSprite ignores crop/anchor in its HitTest. These are observed defects; no core/plugin C# HitTest consumer was found beyond implementations/interfaces. Ordinary voxel picking uses disambiguators.
acceptanceCases: BLIT-04: overlapping cells blend once after masking, with empty cells retained as NullSprite.
PICK-01: never infer browser opaque-pixel selection from this native HitTest; record a corrected coordinate/key policy when implementing it.
steps.disposition: Source expectation; implement and verify in the named slice. Defects require an explicit port decision, not implicit fidelity.

handoffs: Full catalog conversion/effect acceptance stays P2; this review establishes dispatch, loader fallback and native math boundaries, without claiming executed Windows pixel equivalence.
OS DirectDraw/GDI allocation and pixel-format behavior are host boundaries; port sprite behavior through browser rendering, not native DLL execution.

chains.title: Terrain, water, holes, cuts and picking

steps.finding: Full height starts at water level, cuts at zero; suppressing the initial ground surface may start one lower. At surface z, shouldDrawGround queries voxel z with false and z-1 with true (skipping current at topmost world z). Slope flags are fixed at creation from local ground; later ground edits do not recompute these stored flags. Per-cell baseZ<ground chooses underground art independently.
acceptanceCases: CUT-01: paired rail/filler/support occupancy at mixed above/below-ground ramp; verify ground at both boundaries.
CUT-02: terrain changes after slope creation must explicitly address stored flags; topmost/zero-z boundaries retain caller guards.
steps.disposition: Source expectation; implement and verify in the named slice. Defects require an explicit port decision, not implicit fidelity.

steps.finding: Drawer top cut diff is 1; MountainVoxel decrements it to 0 and draws a flat cap, unlike BridgePierVoxel whose alpha-at-zero branch stays unreachable. Mountain transparent iff heightData==0; trees still draw after ground without using cut diff internally. PThreeDimStructure uses strict zdiff<heightCutDiff, otherwise base-layer silhouette. Ground selection uses winter crop only in winter; water full-surface color is night-mapped separately.
acceptanceCases: CUT-03: top-cut mountain -> flat palette cap; same-level pier -> ordinary draw; do not globally subtract one for all voxel kinds.
CUT-04: cut within station footprint -> Gray base silhouette; full/top-above structure -> authored sprite.
CUT-05: full-height water shape, underwater ground chip and underground cut chip remain separate branches.
steps.disposition: Source expectation; implement and verify in the named slice. Defects require an explicit port decision, not implicit fidelity.

steps.finding: Picking scans cut down to zero over projected candidates; rail disambiguator accepts any rail or z<=ground, ground accepts equality, same-level accepts only its anchor z. No alpha test is involved. Tunnel removal reconstructs corner heights only, not removed trees/ownership; tunnel invalidate skips a concealed cell when another tunnel exists on its S/W side.
acceptanceCases: PICK-02: identical screen coordinate with rail/ground/same-level tools can resolve to different z.
TUNNEL-01: restore four heights after removal without asserting restoration of vegetation or ownership; existing endpoint exclusion remains GEO-006.
steps.disposition: Source expectation; implement and verify in the named slice. Defects require an explicit port decision, not implicit fidelity.

handoffs: Terrain editing/growth algorithm and complete structure/catalog rules remain P3/P7. Reviewed here only where they affect occupancy, ground visibility, cut or picking expectations.
Full-world renderer comparisons remain implementation/runtime acceptance, separate from source review.

chains.title: Platform discovery, station ownership and disconnection

steps.finding: Range 8 means an inclusive rectangle around location and otherEnd plus z +/-1, and full-height scans along actual length cells. Station.get identifies station through occupied structure voxels, not distance from station origin. Candidates are deduplicated by unordered Hashtable set. Constructor auto-selects only the first Station candidate, never a platform candidate; it does not guarantee nearest station. Properties can explicitly select a connected platform.
acceptanceCases: HOST-01: base (10,10,2), E length4 -> otherEnd(14,10,2), local rectangle x=2..22,y=2..18,z=1..3; full-height columns x=10..13,y=10.
HOST-02: two stations in range -> do not assert nearest or stable ordering; no direct station but connected platform -> constructor remains disconnected until explicit host choice.
steps.disposition: Source expectation; implement and verify in the named slice. Defects require an explicit port decision, not implicit fidelity.

steps.finding: Changing a host removes this node from the previous parent, clears its host, recursively disconnects copied child nodes, then accepts the new parent only if it resolves a station. It does not auto-reattach children or seek another nearby host. Station removal first removes station-list entry, notifies listeners, disconnects children, then removes structure voxels. No cycle validation in host setter: properties can offer a connected descendant, then cascade clears its station and prevents adoption.
acceptanceCases: HOST-03: S->A->B->C; remove S or detach A -> all descendants disconnected; no implicit nearest-station recovery.
HOST-04: switch A from S1 to S2 -> A resolves S2, B/C remain disconnected until explicitly reattached.
HOST-05: attempt parent A -> its descendant B: clearing A disconnects B before value.hostStation check; B is not adopted.
steps.disposition: Source expectation; implement and verify in the named slice. Defects require an explicit port decision, not implicit fidelity.

steps.finding: Removal restores normal rails and disconnects host tree; fat also removes dedicated platform voxels and restores attached lanes. canRemove guards cars but domain remove relies on callers (fat only asserts). Base removal unregisters daily upkeep and emits entity removal. Yard returns zero without a resolved host station, so loss of host immediately removes station stop/boarding/bell behavior.
acceptanceCases: HOST-06: occupied platform removal must be revalidated authoritatively; source caller assumptions do not provide service safety.
HOST-07: disconnected yard returns zero even at valid stop index; no station board/unload/bell callbacks.
steps.disposition: Source expectation; implement and verify in the named slice. Defects require an explicit port decision, not implicit fidelity.

handoffs: Station population/catchment, packed boarding formula, accounting/listeners and save graph are P6/P0-05 handoffs; no whole-station simulation fidelity claimed.

chains.title: Speed-limit lifecycle, controllers, callbacks and outside return

steps.finding: Menu contribution construction subscribes world change; World.setWorld assigns current world then invokes event, which loads or creates the dictionary entry. getInstance is not lazy; missing contribution or late init leaves null until another world-change event. Retain bundled startup dependency explicitly; do not move semantic initialization behind opening the speed-limit UI.
acceptanceCases: TIME-01: contributions initialized -> select world A -> current-world speed lists; select B -> its lists, never A's singleton.
TIME-02: init after world selection without a new event -> null singleton in source; port must define safe lifecycle independent of menu opening.
steps.disposition: Source expectation; implement and verify in the named slice. Defects require an explicit port decision, not implicit fidelity.

steps.finding: Controller result is not pure in every case. TAT reverse2/rforwarding2 call checkTurn, which reverses immediately, can return early without restoring, and can remove/re-place individual cars without timer unregister. Train then processes returned negative value again. First call checks only pass/stop and waits 10 by default; later calls scan stored rule order for go/reverse/stop/forwarding and poll next ten-minute boundary. TimeMask.nextMatch is not used.
acceptanceCases: TIME-03: preserve distinct 30-minute simple, 5-minute manual and 10-minute TAT defaults.
TIME-04: positive wait bypasses speed limits; -999/-1000 skip boarding but bell after a previous wait; zero first call passes without boarding.
TIME-05: reverse2/rforwarding2 on curve, diagonal one-car and straight consist: account for handler-side mutation before central reversal and stale captured head; explicit port decision required.
steps.disposition: Source expectation; implement and verify in the named slice. Defects require an explicit port decision, not implicit fidelity.

steps.finding: If both forward and reversed calcNextTrainCarState return null, state becomes emergency stop but next.isOutside then throws before scheduling retry. A nonnull blocked candidate does schedule using captured old Inside location; after reversal that still denotes original head, not new head. Outside countdown/failure/return bypass local limits until a subsequent callback starting Inside. Forwarding resets only in nonpositive Inside branch, so any non-yard zero-stop rail clears it; do not assume forwarding lasts to next station.
acceptanceCases: TIME-06: no connected track either way -> null candidate fault in source; safe service behavior must be specified explicitly.
TIME-07: blocked nonnull candidate retains occupancy, no move charge, limit from captured old location; post-reversal location stays old head for limit lookup.
TIME-08: Outside100->...->50 unload/reload unless forwarding; zero attempts return next callback, failure resets10; first connected candidate occupied blocks without trying later candidates.
steps.disposition: Source expectation; implement and verify in the named slice. Defects require an explicit port decision, not implicit fidelity.

steps.finding: Delegation returns first non-singleton controller including null. Named group constructor (used by World root) leaves controller null; unconditional default fallback is false for this chain unless a controller is assigned. TrainItem.moveUnder has no domain cycle guard; malformed groups can loop. Preserve these as source gaps, not guaranteed defaulting.
acceptanceCases: TIME-09: explicitly configured ancestor resolves; all-delegating finite chain reaches default; null ancestor returns null in source and consumer fails.
TIME-10: validate group parent/controller references before authoritative mutation; imported malformed graphs belong to P0-05/P10.
steps.disposition: Source expectation; implement and verify in the named slice. Defects require an explicit port decision, not implicit fidelity.

handoffs: Full timetable configuration/import and manual input UX remain P5/P9; source producers and mutation boundaries reviewed here, not all UI controls.
Queue cancellation remains GEO-002; zero/past intervals and callback exceptions need P1 decisions. Save schema/callback restoration remains P0-05/P10.
